question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q6b(ii)/Q6c(ii) — Rn-222 Decay Values and Half-Life Mass Calculation
question.text:
Radon-222 is a radioactive nuclide which decays spontaneously with the emission of an alpha particle to form Polonium (Po). The nuclear equation is:

²²²₈₆Rn → ᴬZPo + ⁴₂α

(b)(ii) Determine the values of A and Z in the nuclear equation above. (2 marks)

A fresh sample of Radon-222 gas, which has a half-life of 3.8 days, was found to have a mass of 240 g.

(c)(ii) Calculate the mass of Radon-222 gas remaining after 15.2 days, giving your answer to two significant figures. (3 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Q6b(ii) — Decay values:

Conservation of mass number (A): 222 = A + 4 → A = 218

Conservation of atomic number (Z): 86 = Z + 2 → Z = 84

The product is Polonium-218 (²¹⁸₈₄Po).

Q6c(ii) — Half-life mass calculation:

Number of half-lives: n = 15.2 / 3.8 = 4 half-lives

Mass remaining = 240 × (½)⁴ = 240 × (1/16) = 240 / 16 = 15 g

steps.label:
Alpha decay: ²²²₈₆Rn → ᴬ_ZPo + ⁴₂α | Conservation: A_before = A_after; Z_before = Z_after
Half-life: t½ = 3.8 days, initial mass = 240 g, time elapsed = 15.2 days
Determine A (mass number) and Z (atomic number) for Polonium. (2 marks)
Calculate the mass of Rn-222 remaining after 15.2 days (to 2 s.f.). (3 marks)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Conserve mass number: A_Rn = A_Po + A_α → 222 = A + 4 → A = 218.
Conserve atomic number (proton number): Z_Rn = Z_Po + Z_α → 86 = Z + 2 → Z = 84. An alpha particle has Z = 2 (2 protons).
Number of half-lives = time elapsed ÷ half-life = 15.2 ÷ 3.8 = 4.

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Use: remaining mass = initial mass × (½)ⁿ, where n is the number of half-lives.
error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: mass = 240 × (½)⁴ = 240 × (1/16) = 15 g. Each half-life halves the mass: 240 → 120 → 60 → 30 → 15 g.
